# The week

## The week of a retail bank

*How are card, online and branch events spread over the days of the week?*

Share of each channel's events falling on each day of the week:

| Day | Card | Online | Branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 14% | 15% | 22% |
| Tuesday | 14% | 15% | 21% |
| Wednesday | 14% | 15% | 18% |
| Thursday | 14% | 15% | 19% |
| Friday | 15% | 14% | 19% |
| Saturday | 15% | 14% | 0.0% |
| Sunday | 14% | 12% | 0.1% |

On cards, the busiest day of the week carries 1.10×
the events of the quietest.

Intervals (client bootstrap) for the card shares:
Monday 95% CI 13% to 14%;
Tuesday 95% CI 13% to 14%;
Wednesday 95% CI 14% to 14%;
Thursday 95% CI 14% to 15%;
Friday 95% CI 14% to 15%;
Saturday 95% CI 15% to 16%;
Sunday 95% CI 14% to 15%.

Context: n = 947 clients, 54,852 events; 2023-10-02 to 2024-10-02; real extract, allow-listed aggregate; data fingerprint 85887a44d747.

Method: Share of each channel's events falling on each ISO weekday (int_events, exact repeats excluded); client bootstrap intervals.

Caveats:

- Dates may be posting dates rather than transaction dates, so weekend activity can surface on the next working day.
- Branches are closed at weekends; branch shares on those days show where postings land.

Limitation of every calendar result: the extract covers a single year, so the effect of a month,
or of a period such as Ramadan, cannot be separated from the trend over that year (see
[the calendar model's design record](../adr/0009-calendar-model-terms.md)). The weekday shares
above are not affected, because every weekday occurs about equally often over a year; the month
and period effects stay in the private ledger.
